Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:05:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: sudden P95 and throughput drop impacting checkout flows

Vanessa — quick status from infra: we saw a concurrent bump in kernel preemption and a GC pause pattern on the gen runtime on pool-ddb-3 (region-us-west2) starting 06:48. Autoscaler did not spin fast enough because request sizes (seq len) spiked for Checkoutly (they had a batch of long invoices this morning).

Immediate mitigations applied (08:00):
- Increased target concurrency for pool-ddb-3 by +30% (manual override).
- Flushed and warmed KV prefixes for Checkoutly keyspace to reduce cold reads.
- Enabled aggressive batching bypass for short-tail requests to keep latency-sensitive traffic moving (this is a riskier toggle; noted below).

Preliminary impact: p95 improved from ~2.9s -> ~1.6s in the last 10m but throughput still ~12% below expected. Eviction logs show transient token eviction during the spike (we'll pull the full logs).

Short followups we need to coordinate:
- A short-term fallback to a quantized model variant (Q8) will drop cost and reduce token compute but may change output variance; we should get product OK to propose this to Checkoutly.
- Product/Model: any config we can change server-side that requires no client opt-in? Otherwise we'll need customer permission for failover.

I'm pulling logs and will attach the playbook and a short technical summary in 20m.

Ben Carter
SRE — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: sudden P95 and throughput drop impacting checkout flows

Thanks Ben — useful detail. Product asks and recommended customer-facing approach:

Product asks (short runway):
- Approve temporary allowance for model failover: opt customer into Q8 quantized variant (same weights, lower precision) for up to 4 hours. This preserves semantics for most prompts but may affect edge-case formatting.
- Add a small request-size cap via routing policy for Checkoutly (e.g., max tokens per request 1024) while we stabilize. This can be enforced server-side as a routing rule (no SDK change required).
- Track quality regressions: add a small eval set (5 prompts) from Checkoutly to hit on the fallback; if we see >8% semantic drift we roll back and coordinate next step.

Customer note (proposed, please edit):
"Hi Naveen — we implemented mitigation steps and saw initial p95 improvement. To fully stabilize throughput we’d like to temporarily route Checkoutly traffic to a quantized model variant and enforce a short token cap for 4 hours. This is reversible and we’ll monitor quality closely. Do we have permission to proceed?"

I think that message is honest and gives them a clear opt-in. Vanessa — can you send this with Ben’s technical dial included? We should offer a quick impact/rollback bullet and an ETA for follow-up (60–90m).

Karthik Iyer
PM — Runtime & Ops
Redwood Inference

Naveen — quick update and proposed next step: we applied a set of mitigations and have seen p95 improve to ~1.4s; throughput is recovering but not fully back yet. Our SRE team recommends a short, customer-authorized failover to a quantized model variant for up to 4 hours plus a temporary server-side token cap while we finish root-cause analysis.

Proposed wording (can you confirm):
- What we’ll change: route your traffic to a lower-precision (quantized) model variant for up to 4 hours and apply a short token cap (1024 tokens) server-side. This does not require SDK changes.
- Expected impact: faster p95 and improved throughput. Expected semantic impact is minor for typical prompts; we will monitor the five evaluation prompts shared with us and will roll back immediately if we see regressions.
- Rollback and ETA: we will revert within 30 minutes on request. Next status update in 60 minutes.

Attachments: stabilization_playbook.pdf (internal runbook), checkoutly_customer_note_v1.txt (message draft).

Please reply with YES to authorize the temporary failover or NO to decline. If we don't hear back in 15 minutes we'll assume you want us to proceed with the mitigations due to the immediate conversion impact.

Thanks — Vanessa Ortiz
Account Exec, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
